diagnostic_evidence.quote: where \(B\) is the \(N \times N\) diagonal random sampling matrix with i.i.d. Bernoulli random variables with success probability \(m/N\)

issues.failure_explanation: A Bernoulli diagonal matrix has a random number of non-zero rows, not exactly m_i. Therefore B_i as “the m_i non-zero rows of B” is not well-defined for the fixed sketch size required by Algorithm Alg-SRHT; the construction gives a random-size sketch instead of an m_i x N SRHT matrix.

failure_location.quote: which is consisted of the \(m_i\) non-zero rows of \(B\)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the Bernoulli diagonal/retain-nonzero-rows step by a fixed-size row-selection matrix with exactly m_i non-zero rows, or condition on and select exactly m_i rows, so that S_i is an m_i x N SRHT matrix as assumed.
issues.overall_effect: The implemented algorithm does not reliably provide the fixed-size sketches S_i assumed by the convergence and complexity theorems.
issues.title: SRHT row construction does not yield a fixed-size sketch
issues.why_classification: The fix is a local construction correction to a standard fixed-size SRHT; it does not change the advertised convergence rate or complexity if the theorems are then applied to the corrected sketches.

issues.failure_explanation: The matrices U_X^T hatS^T hatS U_X and U_X^T S_i^T S_i U_X are symmetric positive definite but need not commute. Hence W_i = I_d - mu A^{-1}B_i is not symmetric in general and does not admit an orthonormal eigendecomposition with tilde U_i^T. The subsequent block diagonalization and norm contraction are therefore not justified as written.

failure_location.quote: Let the eigenvalue decomposition of \(W_i\) be \(W_i = \tilde{U}_i \Lambda_i \tilde{U}_i^{\top}\)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must justify the spectral or norm behavior of the nonnormal iteration matrix W_i, for example by proving a bounded-condition-number similarity to a symmetric matrix, adding hypotheses making W_i normal, or establishing the 1/3 contraction by another valid argument.
issues.overall_effect: The per-stage 1/3 contraction and all downstream convergence, stopping-count, and complexity results that rely on it are unsupported.
issues.title: Contraction proof assumes an orthogonal eigendecomposition of a generally non-symmetric matrix
issues.why_classification: The central convergence rate is obtained from an invalid spectral step; preserving the stated rate would require new nontrivial analysis or stronger assumptions not present in the source.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem statement gives r(i-1,i) as sqrt(m_{i-1} - d/m_i - d), which is not the fraction used in the proof and is numerically/dimensionally ill-defined. The proof uses sqrt((m_i-d)/(m_{i-1}-d)), while the complexity proof uses the reciprocal ratio. There is no single source-consistent definition supporting the stated lower bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the definition of r(i-1,i) consistently with the derivation; the proof uses sqrt((m_i-d)/(m_{i-1}-d)), and downstream formulas using the opposite ratio must be updated.
issues.overall_effect: The lower bound on the required iteration counts a_i and any stopping rule or complexity derived from it are unreliable.
issues.title: Ill-defined and inconsistent r(i-1,i) in the lower bound for a_i
issues.why_classification: The defect is more than a typo because there are incompatible mathematical definitions and the repair changes the a_i bound and downstream complexity; nevertheless a contained correction and re-derivation of the affected formula avoids new architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: To dominate the previous-stage sketched error by the current one, the lower-bound derivation requires r(i-1,i)=sqrt((m_i-d)/(m_{i-1}-d)), which tends to sqrt(2). The complexity proof instead uses the reciprocal ratio tending to 1/sqrt(2), yielding an alpha that is too small and a first-stage cost bound 4 alpha Nd that is not supported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 1/sqrt(2) by sqrt(2) in alpha, or prove the reciprocal-ratio bound, and recompute the first-stage cost with the corrected alpha.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised asymptotic upper bound on a_i and the first-stage FLOP estimate for Algorithm Alg-SRHT are false as stated.
issues.title: Complexity theorem uses the reciprocal r(i-1,i) and an unsupported alpha
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained correction of a quantitative complexity constant and upper bound; it does not require a new proof architecture, but it materially changes the stated alpha and cost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: To minimize the cost of Algorithm \ref{Alg-SRHT} in this discussion, we let $T = \log_3(1/\sigma)$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof chooses T=log_3(1/sigma) and writes T-T^dagger=log_3(1/sigma)-sum a_i, but the algorithm and convergence statements require T>T^dagger+M. The condition omega>sigma^{1/K} only ensures log_3(1/sigma)>K log_3(1/omega), not log_3(1/sigma)>sum a_i+M, since a_i may be much larger than the lower bounds. Thus T-T^dagger can be negative or the required M full-stage iterations can dominate, so the stated second-stage cost is unsupported.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a feasibility condition such as sum a_i+M<log_3(1/sigma), or define T=max{log_3(1/sigma), sum a_i+M} and restate the second-stage cost with a positive-part or max expression including the required M iterations.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed dominant cost of the full-scale stage of Algorithm Alg-SRHT is not guaranteed by the proof.
issues.title: Second-stage iteration count and cost derivation is not feasible as stated
issues.why_classification: The gap is a missing condition and an incorrect iteration-count calculation in the complexity proof; a local corrected complexity statement can preserve an O(Nd) cost, but the advertised exact dominant term requires repair.
